title: Persisting the loop's dispatch cursor no longer fails with a 500
description: On a real temporary Postgres behind the served API, a second writer persists the dispatch cursor while another writer (the old loop beside a restarted one) is mid-way through its own write and the wait outlives the server's timeout. The loser is answered with a 409 conflict instead of a 500, the loop's client retries it so the stored cursor is the later write, and a loop cycle racing that other writer completes its dispatch step.

steps.name: Two writers of the dispatch cursor get a conflict and a retry, never a 500
